subject: SpectraAI reserved GPU commitment & isolation ops plan
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex@spectraai.com>, Jordan Park <jordan.park@spectraai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: SpectraAI post-call: isolation requirements, throughput targets, next steps

Hi Alex & Jordan,

Thanks again for the time today — good discussion. Below is a short recap of the pain points you called out, our mutual goals, and the immediate next steps we agreed on. I want to make sure we captured everything before Ben and I start sizing a reserved pool proposal.

1) Primary pain points you shared
- Latency spikes during peak reporting windows (batch inference) causing timeouts for customer-facing scoring flows.
- Regulatory need for tenant isolation for PHI-containing models (separate GPU tenancy + audit logs).
- Predictability of unit cost — you need a bounded monthly spend for forecasting, not a per-token surprise.

2) Goals / success metrics
- Tail latency (p95) below 120ms for short-chat calls, 95th percentile for scoring < 300ms during peak.
- Dedicated compute for PHI workloads with tenancy isolation and KMS-integrated key management.
- SLA target: 99.9% monthly uptime for critical inference endpoints; recovery playbook for degraded capacity.

3) Proposed Redwood approach (high level)
- Reserved GPU pool (dedicated) sized for sustained throughput + configured burst slots for uneven spikes.
- Isolation: tenant-siloing on the pool with per-tenant network segmentation and audit log retention (90 days standard, longer on request).
- Cost predictability: monthly reserved commitment + optional burst billing cap.

4) Immediate next steps (owners & timeline)
- Ben: produce a preliminary pool sizing and cost estimate (capacity + burst) by Tuesday 5/26.
- Sean/Marissa: technical appendix (KV cache, quantization options, expected latency at different sequence lengths) by Wednesday 5/27.
- Alex: share your 7-day peak token/sec sample and SOC2 questionnaire responses (Jordan will route to procurement).
- Joint: schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra and data-security teams the week of 6/1.

Attachments: I attached a quick MOP (operational playbook) sketch and a draft SLA we can iterate on.

If anything above is off, call it out and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll share Ben’s sizing and Marissa’s latency appendix early next week.

Thanks,

Sean Gallagher

Thanks Sean — that aligns well. A couple of clarifications before you size: 

- For isolation, we need a hard boundary for PHI models (no shared CUDA processes). Can you confirm the dedicated pool will provide single-tenant GPUs rather than multi-tenant VM slices?
- For burst handling: during daily report runs we can see 6-8x baseline sustained QPS for ~10–20 minutes. Any built-in throttling/fallback you recommend?

Jordan will attach the 7-day token/sec export and our procurement onboarding doc in a follow-up. We have a procurement window closing 6/15 (preferred) but could stretch if technical gating takes longer.

—Alex

alex@spectraai.com

Subject: Re: SpectraAI post-call: isolation requirements, throughput targets, next steps

Alex — quick answers and what I’ll include in the sizing PDF: 

1) Isolation model: reserved GPU pool provides single-tenant allocation (one customer per GPU instance). For strict PHI separation we propose a reserved node group that is never colocated. We’ll document process for visual verification during onboarding.

2) Burst strategy: we recommend a hybrid of burst slots + automatic read-only fallback to a lower-cost model variant to prevent timeouts. Burst slots are pre-warmed GPUs that can be consumed for short windows (configurable limit). If burst capacity is exhausted, Redwood’s routing will spill to approved compatible variants (you define the policy).

3) Latency estimates: I’ll include p50/p95 estimates for the three operating points you mentioned (baseline, 4x, 8x) based on similar workloads.

Deliverables by 5/26: sizing.pdf (pool vCPU/GPU counts, burst slot count, monthly committed cost and burst cap model).

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
